assets.source: a16z-infra/ai-town stock demo character texture; historically mapped from data/characters.ts (removed from this repo by ART-112) to data/spritesheets/f1.ts..f8.ts frame data
assets.author: Unresolved -- ART-143 re-opened this against primary sources and still could not attribute the texture to any named artist, asset pack or generator
assets.notes: Byte-identical to upstream (sha256 4f82a3bf6f037698ad94ae4b7309a43bd68e2397a04891de9717edc56e7630d5). ART-143 investigation, primary sources only: (1) upstream a16z-infra/ai-town has exactly two commits touching this path, a41c22089 'New 32x32 spritesheet' (2023-08-12T16:52:25Z) and dca78f5ea 'New 32x32 characters' (2023-08-12T21:40:38Z, PR #54 'Martin character'), both by 61cygni -- the two versions are entirely different character art at the same 384x256 layout, i.e. upstream swapped the whole cast within five hours, and neither commit, the PR body nor its review comment names a source. (2) Upstream's README 'Other credits' names a third-party source for every other art category it uses (two OpenGameArt tilesets, ansimuz, Mounir Tohami's UI pack, MusicGen audio) but names none for the character spritesheet; its only adjacent line, 'Pixel Art Generation: Replicate, Fal.ai', was added 48 minutes after this file landed by a different author (PR #50, a generic Stack bullet) and is never linked to this file. (3) The PNG carries no author, copyright or generator metadata -- only sRGB, an eXIf orientation tag, pHYs, and boilerplate Adobe XMP holding just tiff:Orientation. (4) Upstream issue #202 asked where these textures come from and the maintainer answered only with the directory path, recording no licence or attribution. (5) No visual or catalogue match was found against candidate 32x32 character packs (Pipoya, OpenGameArt CC0 sets, itch.io and RPG-Maker-style packs); exact-string web search for '32x32folk' returns nothing. Conclusion: redistribution and modification rights cannot be confirmed from primary evidence, so this stays quarantined. Upstream's root MIT LICENSE is a real grant but only carries rights upstream actually held, and nothing establishes that for this file. Resolving it needs an owner-level licence decision (ART-143, blocker H06), not more research -- PRD 2.0 section 6 lists sourcing a replacement external asset pack or an image-generation model as a v1 non-goal, so re-sourcing is not available without a PRD exception.
